name: Six Sigma and Organizational Goals
description: Why organisations use Six Sigma and where it came from (Shewhart, Deming, Juran, Ishikawa), linking projects to organisational goals with SMART objectives, and the business drivers, KPIs and scorecards projects affect.
l1: Explains the value of Six Sigma, how a project links to organisational goals, and how drivers such as profit, market share and customer satisfaction show in KPIs and scorecards (Yellow Belt).
l2: Ties their own project to a strategic goal with SMART objectives and shows its effect on the organisation's KPIs and scorecard (Green Belt).
l3: Aligns a portfolio of projects with strategy and the scorecard, and leads deployment in a function (Black Belt).
l4: Designs an organisation's Six Sigma deployment, linking project selection to strategy and setting the metrics leadership reviews (Master Black Belt).
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Lean Principles in the Organization
description: Lean concepts (theory of constraints, value chain, flow, takt time, just-in-time, gemba, spaghetti diagrams, perfection) and value stream mapping to separate value-added steps from waste.
l1: Understands lean concepts such as flow, pull, takt time, just-in-time and the theory of constraints, and the types of waste.
l2: Uses a value stream map, spaghetti diagram or gemba walk on their own process to find waste and constraints, and applies takt time and flow.
l3: Leads lean redesign of whole value streams with future-state maps and coaches teams to deliver them.
l4: Sets an organisation's lean strategy and trains and certifies its Black Belts and lean leaders.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Design for Six Sigma (DFSS) Methodologies
description: Design for Six Sigma road maps (DMADV, IDOV) and how they relate to DMAIC, verification and validation of designs, and failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), including design and process FMEA.
l1: Understands how DMADV and IDOV differ from DMAIC and what FMEA and risk priority numbers are for.
l2: Runs a design or process FMEA: scores severity, occurrence and detection, calculates risk priority numbers and acts on the highest.
l3: Leads DFSS projects for new products or services through DMADV, including verification and validation against requirements.
l4: Designs an organisation's DFSS programme and mentors its Black Belts in it.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Project Identification
description: Choosing and framing improvement projects: whether DMAIC fits the problem, process boundaries across functions, benchmarking, SIPOC inputs and outputs, and process owners and stakeholders.
l1: Understands how projects are selected, what a SIPOC shows, the types of benchmarking, and who process owners and stakeholders are.
l2: Judges whether a problem suits DMAIC, maps its SIPOC and boundaries, analyses key inputs and outputs, and identifies its owners and stakeholders.
l3: Builds and prioritises a project pipeline for a function from data and benchmarks, and coaches Green Belts in scoping.
l4: Sets project selection criteria and pipeline governance across an organisation.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Voice of the Customer (VoC)
description: Identifying internal and external customers, collecting their views (surveys, focus groups, interviews, observation), and turning requirements into measures with QFD, critical-to-quality trees and the Kano model.
l1: Understands who a project's customers are and how QFD, CTQ trees and the Kano model turn their needs into requirements.
l2: Collects customer data with unbiased questions and translates it into critical-to-quality requirements with a CTQ tree, the Kano model or QFD.
l3: Designs VoC programmes across customer segments and resolves conflicting requirements with weighted QFD.
l4: Shapes how an organisation listens to and acts on its customers, and trains Black Belts in VoC methods.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Project Management Basics
description: Running an improvement project: agile or top-down methods, the charter and problem statement, scope, primary and consequential metrics, WBS, Gantt, CPM and PERT, toll-gate reviews, risk analysis and closure.
l1: Understands the parts of a charter, scoping tools, project metrics, planning tools (WBS, Gantt chart, critical path) and toll-gate reviews.
l2: Writes a charter with a baselined problem statement and goals, plans with a WBS and Gantt chart, runs toll-gate reviews and closes with lessons learned.
l3: Manages several or complex projects, including their risks and resourcing, and coaches Green Belts through their tollgates.
l4: Sets project governance and toll-gate standards for a Six Sigma programme.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Management and Planning Tools
description: The management and planning tools: affinity diagrams, interrelationship digraphs, tree diagrams, prioritisation matrices, matrix diagrams, process decision program charts, activity network diagrams and SWOT analysis.
l1: Recognises the management and planning tools and what each is for.
l2: Selects and uses these tools on a project, such as an affinity diagram to group ideas and a prioritisation matrix to choose among solutions.
l3: Facilitates the right tools for complex, cross-functional problems and teaches others to use them.
l4: Standardises and teaches planning-tool use across an organisation's improvement programme.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Business Results for Projects
description: Measuring project results: defects per unit, defects per million opportunities, rolled throughput yield, cost of poor quality, sigma level and capability, and communicating results top-down, bottom-up and across.
l1: Understands DPU, DPMO, rolled throughput yield, cost of poor quality and sigma level.
l2: Calculates DPU, DPMO, rolled throughput yield, cost of poor quality and sigma level for their project, and uses them to drive and report decisions.
l3: Validates financial and process benefits across projects with finance and reports them to leadership.
l4: Sets the benefit measurement and validation rules for an organisation's programme.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Team Dynamics and Performance
description: Team stages (forming to adjourning), negative dynamics such as groupthink, roles set out with RACI, team tools such as brainstorming, nominal group technique and multivoting, and team communication.
l1: Understands team stages, the roles on Six Sigma teams and common negative dynamics.
l2: Leads a project team: sets roles with a RACI, uses brainstorming, nominal group technique and multivoting, and handles negative dynamics.
l3: Builds and coaches teams through difficult dynamics, and coaches Green Belts as team leaders.
l4: Develops team leadership practice for an organisation's improvement programme.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Process Analysis
description: Process analysis and documentation: process maps, flowcharts, written procedures and work instructions, reviewed to find gaps and misaligned steps.
l1: Understands process maps and flowcharts, and how procedures and work instructions document a process.
l2: Maps a process and reviews its procedures and work instructions to find gaps, redundant steps and misalignment.
l3: Analyses complex cross-functional processes and guides others' mapping.
l4: Sets process documentation standards for an organisation.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Probability and Statistics
description: Basic probability (independent and mutually exclusive events, multiplication rules, permutations and combinations) and the central limit theorem's role in confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and control charts.
l1: Understands basic probability rules, permutations and combinations, and why the central limit theorem underpins confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and control charts.
l2: Applies probability rules and the central limit theorem to project data, for example to set sample sizes or interpret subgroup averages.
l3: Applies statistical reasoning to complex problems and reviews others' analyses for errors.
l4: Teaches statistical foundations to Black Belts and sets an organisation's analysis standards.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Statistical Distributions
description: The common distributions (normal, binomial, Poisson, chi-square, Student's t and F) and where each applies in statistical process control and inference.
l1: Understands the normal, binomial, Poisson, chi-square, t and F distributions and where each applies.
l2: Chooses the right distribution for project data (binomial for defectives, Poisson for defect counts) and uses it in tests and limits.
l3: Handles non-normal data with transformations or other distributions, and guides others' distributional analysis.
l4: Teaches distribution theory to Black Belts and sets an organisation's analysis standards.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Collecting and Summarizing Data
description: Data types and measurement scales, sampling and data collection plans (random and stratified sampling, check sheets), descriptive statistics, and graphs such as histograms, box plots and normal probability plots.
l1: Understands continuous and discrete data, nominal to ratio scales, and basic summaries.
l2: Writes a data collection plan with sampling and data quality checks, then summarises the data with descriptive statistics, histograms, box plots and probability plots.
l3: Designs sampling and data collection for complex studies and coaches others in it.
l4: Sets data collection standards for an organisation's programme.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Measurement System Analysis
description: Measurement system analysis: gauge repeatability and reproducibility, bias, linearity, measurement correlation, percent agreement for attribute data, and precision-to-tolerance ratio.
l1: Understands why a measurement system must be checked before its data are trusted.
l2: Runs and interprets a gauge R&R study or attribute agreement analysis, and acts on bias, linearity or precision-to-tolerance results.
l3: Designs MSA for complex, destructive or attribute measurement systems and guides others.
l4: Sets measurement system standards for an organisation and trains others.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Process and Performance Capability
description: Process capability: natural process limits versus specification limits, capability studies, Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk and Cpm indices, sigma level, and short-term versus long-term capability and sigma shift.
l1: Understands what capability and performance indices measure and how they differ.
l2: Runs a capability study, checking stability and normality first, then calculates and interprets Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk and sigma level.
l3: Assesses capability for non-normal, multi-stream or short-run processes and advises on specification limits.
l4: Sets capability requirements and methods for an organisation and its suppliers.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Exploratory Data Analysis
description: Exploring sources of variation: multi-vari studies (positional, cyclical, temporal) and correlation and simple linear regression, telling correlation from causation.
l1: Understands multi-vari charts, correlation and regression, and that correlation is not causation.
l2: Uses multi-vari studies, correlation and simple linear regression to find likely sources of variation, and interprets their significance.
l3: Applies multiple regression and other exploratory methods to complex data and guides others' analyses.
l4: Sets exploratory analysis practice for an organisation and teaches it to Black Belts.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Hypothesis Testing
description: Hypothesis testing: statistical versus practical significance, significance level, power and sample size, type I and II errors, and tests for means, variances and proportions (t, F, ANOVA, chi-square).
l1: Understands null and alternative hypotheses, p-values, type I and II errors and power.
l2: Selects and runs t-tests, paired t-tests, F-tests, one-way ANOVA and chi-square tests with suitable sample sizes, and interprets the results.
l3: Designs test strategies for complex questions, including power, multiple comparisons and non-parametric tests, and reviews others' tests.
l4: Teaches statistical inference to Black Belts and reviews high-stakes analyses for an organisation.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Additional Analysis Methods
description: Gap analysis between current and future states, and root cause analysis with cause-and-effect diagrams, relational matrices, 5 Whys and fault tree analysis.
l1: Understands gap analysis and root cause tools such as cause-and-effect diagrams and 5 Whys.
l2: Uses gap analysis and root cause tools (cause-and-effect diagram, 5 Whys, fault tree) to find and verify the true cause of a problem.
l3: Leads root cause analysis on complex, multi-cause problems and guides others.
l4: Standardises root cause methods across an organisation and trains others in them.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Design of Experiments (DoE)
description: Design of experiments: factors, levels, responses, treatments, blocking, randomisation and replication, and reading main effects and interaction plots.
l1: Understands what designed experiments are for and their basic terms.
l2: Runs a simple designed experiment with randomised, replicated runs and interprets main effects and interaction plots.
l3: Designs and analyses full and fractional factorial experiments, including blocking, confounding and resolution, and guides others.
l4: Teaches experimentation to Black Belts and reviews complex designs for an organisation.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Implementation Planning
description: Planning how improvements are put in place: proofs of concept, try-storming, simulations and pilot tests before full roll-out.
l1: Understands why improvements are piloted before roll-out.
l2: Plans and runs a pilot, simulation or try-storming of an improvement and uses the results to plan the roll-out.
l3: Leads large implementations and the change management they need, and guides others' pilots.
l4: Sets implementation practice for an organisation's improvement programme.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Lean Tools
description: Lean tools for improvement: waste elimination (pull, kanban, 5S, standard work, poka-yoke), cycle-time reduction (continuous flow, SMED), and kaizen and kaizen blitz.
l1: Recognises the main lean tools and the waste each removes.
l2: Applies 5S, kanban, poka-yoke, standard work or SMED to a process and runs a kaizen event.
l3: Leads kaizen programmes and lean redesigns across areas and coaches others.
l4: Sets lean tool standards and trains practitioners across an organisation.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Statistical Process Control (SPC)
description: Statistical process control: common- and special-cause variation, rational subgrouping, and selecting and reading control charts (X-bar and R, X-bar and s, ImR, median, p, np, c and u).
l1: Understands what control charts show and the difference between common and special causes.
l2: Selects, builds and interprets the right control chart for the data with rational subgroups, and reacts to out-of-control signals.
l3: Designs SPC for complex processes, including charts for short runs or small shifts (such as EWMA or CUSUM) and reaction plans, and reviews others' charts.
l4: Sets SPC standards for an organisation and trains others.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Sustain Improvements
description: Sustaining improvements: control plans, document control, training plans, first-, second- and third-party audits, and plan-do-check-act.
l1: Understands why gains need control plans, document control, training and audits.
l2: Writes a control plan and training plan, updates controlled documents and hands the improved process to its owner.
l3: Makes sure gains last across projects with audits and plan-do-check-act reviews, and guides others' control plans.
l4: Builds the organisation's systems for sustaining improvement.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black

name: Lean Tools for Process Control
description: Lean tools for process control: total productive maintenance (including predictive maintenance) and the visual factory (andon, jidoka).
l1: Understands the elements of TPM and the visual factory (andon, jidoka) and how they hold an improved process.
l2: Uses TPM and visual controls such as andon to keep an improved process stable.
l3: Leads TPM and visual management across an area and coaches others.
l4: Sets TPM and visual management standards for an organisation.
source: Drafted for the graph from the ASQ CSSGB Body of Knowledge (2022); belts by role, Yellow to Master Black
